name: Mamasa
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_quote: In this section we will first examine word stress and then intonation. 4.1 Stress. Stress in Mamasa is not phonemic. Normally the penultimate syllable of a word is stressed (except in the case of the rather rare one-syllable word). ... There is one exception to this stress rule. Vocatives are always stressed on the final syllable of the word.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passages are verbatim in the Matti 1991 PDF we hold at printed pp. 66-67 (pp. 14-15), exactly as the record's the domain quotation/the domain locator/sources state. (2) The classification fixed-strict penultimate (penultimate stress) at word domain is exactly what Matti describes: non-phonemic penultimate stress, recomputed over suffixes, not over enclitics, with final stress only in vocatives (a morphologically conditioned exception, not a lexical contrast) and /ai/ behaving as a diphthong before possessive suffixes (bái-ku), which Matti handles by ordering diphthongisation before stress (p.60-61, section 6). None of this disturbs the classification. (3) Deciding source is a dedicated 1991 SIL phonology article by the language's principal describer; Glottolog lists no grammar, dissertation, or later phonology for Mamasa, so it is the best available and it is. tone.quote: The study of Pattae language conservation aimed to describe the specific language system in terms of speech sounds, including vowel and consonant segmental phonemes as well as voiced and voiceless, by finding their minimum pairs. Thus, it was formulated to describe segmental phonemes on vowel-consonant sound classification and Pattae language map and how to describe minimum pairs of vowel-consonant sound classification of the Pattae language.

sources.note: Pusat Bahasa Struktur Bahasa X reports of this period normally open with a fonologi chapter (fonem segmental, pola suku kata, sometimes tekanan 'stress'); a tone statement is unlikely beyond, at most, a remark that nada/tekanan is not distinctive. Would be a second, non-SIL first-hand phonology of Mamasa predating Matti 1991.
